leads.title: Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810
leads.documents: Decriminalisation of same-sex sexual activity in private in France; retained policy followed in French colonies. Establishes baseline legal status applicable to Mayotte as French territory.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text. Citation detail visible: 'Penal Code of 1791 made no mention of same-sex relations in private' retained in 'Penal Code of 1810'

leads.title: Penal Code Article 330, alinea 2 - Mirguet amendment (Ordonnance of 1960)
leads.documents: 1960 discriminatory indecent exposure clause that doubled penalty for homosexual activity; repealed in 1980 as part of act redefining sexual offenses.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'article 330, 2nd alinea' proposed by Paul Mirguet, adopted 1960, repealed 1980

leads.title: Penal Code Article 334 / Article 331 - Vichy age of consent law
leads.documents: Unequal age of consent (21 then 18 for homosexual relations vs 15 for heterosexual); repealed 4 August 1982 under Mitterrand to equalise at 15.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: introduced 6 August 1942, moved to article 331 on 8 February 1945, lowered to 18 in 1974, repealed 4 August 1982

leads.title: 1985 anti-discrimination law, July 2012 amendment and Law of 18 November 2016 amending Article 225-1 Penal Code
leads.documents: Prohibition of sexual orientation discrimination (1985), addition of 'sexual identity' (2012) replaced by 'gender identity' (2016). Core transgender/LGB employment, housing, goods/services protection machinery.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'article 225-1 of the French Penal Code' amended 18 November 2016 to replace 'sexual identity' with 'gender identity'

leads.title: French Labour Code (Code du travail), Chapter 2
leads.documents: Quoted anti-discrimination provision barring exclusion, sanction or dismissal on account of sexual orientation, gender identity, morals, gender, etc.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: full quoted text starting 'No person may be excluded from a recruitment process...' listing 'sexual orientation, gender identity'

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 and Law on the Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881, Title 3 Articles 20 and 21 - Haute autorité de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'égalité
leads.documents: Criminalisation of homophobic/sexist/racist comments, injury, defamation, incitement to hatred/violence; increased penalties for bias-motivated assault/murder; creation of High Authority against Discrimination and for Equality.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: National Assembly approved amendment 31 Dec 2004, max penalty €45,000 and/or 12 months; Chirac Government justification; first conviction Christian Vanneste Jan 2006 cancelled by Court of Cassation

leads.title: Same-sex marriage law 2013 - National Assembly, Senate and Constitutional Council Decision of 17 May 2013, Journal Officiel 19 May 2013
leads.documents: Legalisation of same-sex marriage and joint adoption in France; article states 'Same-sex marriage is legal in all of France's overseas departments and territories' including Mayotte; notes 2 deputies from Mayotte voted in favor.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Assembly 329-229 on 12 Feb 2013, Senate 179-157 on 9 Apr and approval 12 Apr, Assembly 23 Apr, Council ruled constitutional 17 May 2013, signed 18 May by Hollande, published next day in Journal Officiel, first ceremony 29 May Montpellier

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on legal gender change (effective 1 January 2017) - Constitutional Council ruling 17 November 2016
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without surgery/sterilisation or psychiatrist certificates, via court; first name change via registry office. Key transgender legal-status machinery.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Senate approved 6 Nov 2015, Assembly 24 May 2016 and 12 July 2016 modified version, Senate 28 Sept, Assembly 12 Oct, Council ruled constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov 2016, published Journal Officiel next day, took effect 1 Jan 2017

leads.title: B. vs France - European Court of Human Rights (1992)
leads.documents: Ruling that changed French ban on legal gender change, requiring France to allow legal gender change even after medical/surgical transition.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: '1992 case, B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changed this' after decades-long legislative ban

leads.title: ILGA-Europe report published 2022 on gender affirming healthcare in France
leads.documents: Documents lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable access by location for gender affirming healthcare in France; recommended informed consent/self-determination system.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'A report published in 2022 by ILGA-Europe found significant issues with the provision of gender affirming healthcare in France'
